evals.prompt: Build me a 10-slide deck for my board on why we should acquire competitor X. Audience is non-technical board members.
evals.description: Topic-only deck for a board audience; tests SCQA framing and executive tone.
expected_output_criteria: Opens with a Situation-Complication-Question-Answer (SCQA) flow on slide 1 or 2
Top-line answer slide (recommendation) appears within the first 3 slides per Pyramid Principle
Slides are titled with the takeaway, not the topic (e.g., 'Acquiring X expands our distribution by 40%' not 'Distribution analysis')
Includes speaker notes for each slide written for verbal delivery, not as a transcript of the slide
Avoids technical jargon and product internals; framing stays at board-relevant level (strategy, financials, risk)

evals.prompt: Convert this 60-page PDF [attached] into a 15-slide internal engineering all-hands deck. Don't water down the technical content.
evals.description: Document-to-deck for a technical audience; should keep depth, apply MECE.
expected_output_criteria: Decomposes the PDF content using MECE so slide topics don't overlap and cover the source faithfully
Preserves technical depth (architecture diagrams, metrics, code-level detail) rather than summarising into vague themes
Groups slides into a clear 3-4 act structure (e.g., context → current state → proposal → next steps)
Speaker notes call out points where the presenter should pause for Q&A or expect pushback
Flags any content from the source that was intentionally cut and why

evals.prompt: I have a deck that landed badly with the CFO last week. She said it was 'too long and too vague'. Rebuild it for a 15-minute slot, ruthlessly.
evals.description: Hard scenario: ruthless editing under audience-specific feedback.
expected_output_criteria: Cuts slide count to a number defensible in a 15-minute slot (typically 5-8) and justifies the cut
Restructures around a single CFO-relevant question (cost, ROI, risk) rather than narrating the project
Every slide leads with a number or decision, not background
Provides a 30-second opening line the presenter should use to set the answer up front
Flags any content removed but available as appendix for follow-up Q&A
